subject: Global Perspectives
title: Stage 1 Global Perspectives Readiness Check
description: A short, friendly check of talking, listening, noticing and working with friends, so we can find your perfect starting point.
attemptsAllowed: Unlimited — this exam finds your starting point; it is never a fail
feedbackMode: Immediate child-friendly feedback with a placement report

ready.label: Ready for Stage 1
ready.message: Brilliant work! You can listen, notice things and work with friends. Stage 1, here you come.

readyWithReview.label: Ready — with a little review
readyWithReview.message: You are ready to start Stage 1. Warm up first with the review lessons below.

notReady.label: Let's build strong roots first
notReady.message: Let's practise talking, listening and sharing before Stage 1. A grown-up or teacher can play asking-and-listening games with you every day.

recommendation.label: Stage 1 Global Perspectives, Unit 1 with a grown-up

sections.title: Talking and listening
sections.description: Can you listen carefully, ask good questions and tell others your ideas? These are your first communication and research skills.

sections.title: Noticing and sorting
sections.description: Can you look closely, spot what is the same and different, and put things into groups? These are your first analysis and evaluation skills.

sections.title: Working together
sections.description: Can you share, take turns and think about how a job went? These are your first collaboration and reflection skills.

questions.question: Your teacher is telling the class a story. What does a good listener do?
questions.options: Talk to a friend | Look out of the window | Sing a song | Look at the teacher and listen quietly
questions.correctAnswer: Look at the teacher and listen quietly
questions.explanation: Good listeners keep their eyes on the speaker and their voices quiet, so they hear every word of the story.

questions.question: Amina wants to find out her friend's favourite fruit. What should she do?
questions.options: Ask her friend and listen to the answer | Guess without asking | Ask the wall | Say her own favourite fruit is the answer
questions.correctAnswer: Ask her friend and listen to the answer
questions.explanation: When we want to find something out about a person, we ask them a question and listen carefully to what they say.

questions.question: Yusuf is talking about his grandma. You want to say something too. What should you do?
questions.options: Shout so everyone hears you | Wait for him to finish, then talk | Talk at the same time as him | Walk away
questions.correctAnswer: Wait for him to finish, then talk
questions.explanation: We take turns when we talk. Waiting for your turn shows Yusuf you care about his words, and then everyone can hear yours.

questions.question: Sara drew a picture of her family. She wants to tell the class about it. What is the best way?
questions.options: Hold up the picture and say who is in it | Hide the picture behind her back | Say nothing and sit down | Whisper so nobody can hear
questions.correctAnswer: Hold up the picture and say who is in it
questions.explanation: Showing your picture and talking about it in a clear voice helps everyone see and understand your ideas.

questions.question: Your teacher gives the class a job to do, but you do not understand it. What should you do?
questions.options: Pretend you understood | Do nothing and hope for the best | Copy a friend without asking | Put up your hand and ask the teacher
questions.correctAnswer: Put up your hand and ask the teacher
questions.explanation: Asking a question when you are not sure is a smart thing to do — it is how we learn and get things right.

questions.question: You are sorting things into a toy box and a fruit bowl. Where does a banana go?
questions.options: In the fruit bowl, because it is a fruit | In the toy box, because it is yellow | In both at the same time | Nowhere — throw it away
questions.correctAnswer: In the fruit bowl, because it is a fruit
questions.explanation: Sorting means putting things that belong together in the same group. A banana is a fruit, so it goes with the other fruit.

questions.question: Adam wants to know how many children in his class have a cat at home. What should he do?
questions.options: Count the chairs in the room | Make up a big number | Ask only his best friend | Ask each child and count the answers
questions.correctAnswer: Ask each child and count the answers
questions.explanation: To find out about everyone, Adam asks everyone and counts. That is how we collect answers we can trust.

questions.question: Layla looks at a cat and a bird. Which of these is one way they are DIFFERENT?
questions.options: The bird has wings and the cat does not | They both need food | They are both animals | They are both alive
questions.correctAnswer: The bird has wings and the cat does not
questions.explanation: Looking closely helps us spot differences. Wings belong to the bird only — the other answers are ways the two are the same.

questions.question: Which of these can everyone check by looking, and is not just what one person likes?
questions.options: There are four chairs at the table | Red is the prettiest colour | Bananas taste better than apples | Rainy days are boring
questions.correctAnswer: There are four chairs at the table
questions.explanation: Anyone can count the chairs and see four — that is something we can check. The others are feelings, and different people feel differently.

questions.question: You are building a block tower and your friend wants to help. What is the kind thing to do?
questions.options: Tell your friend to go away | Knock the tower down | Share the blocks and build it together | Hide all the blocks
questions.correctAnswer: Share the blocks and build it together
questions.explanation: Working together means sharing. Two builders can make an even better tower — and building it is more fun with a friend.

questions.question: Bilan and Cali both want the red crayon at the same time. What should they do?
questions.options: Take turns using the red crayon | Break the crayon in half | Both cry loudly | Grab it and pull hard
questions.correctAnswer: Take turns using the red crayon
questions.explanation: Taking turns is fair: one friend uses the crayon first, then the other. Nobody gets hurt and both get to colour in red.

questions.question: Your class made a garden picture together and now it is finished. What is a good thing to think about?
questions.options: Nothing — never think about finished work | Who we can blame for anything wrong | What we did well and what we could do better next time | How to do the same job again right now
questions.correctAnswer: What we did well and what we could do better next time
questions.explanation: Thinking back about a finished job is called reflecting. It helps us feel proud of the good parts and do even better next time.
